title: Time Blocking 101
description: A 5-minute video on reserving realistic blocks of uninterrupted time for important work. Useful when you know your priorities but meetings and small requests keep consuming the hours you intended to spend on them. Covers choosing a focus window, allowing buffer time, and protecting the block.

title: Overcoming Procrastination
description: An interactive worksheet for a task you repeatedly put off, even when time is available. Identify whether uncertainty, perfectionism, or discomfort is making it hard to start, then define a small first action and a concrete starting cue. Useful for getting an avoided piece of work moving.

title: Delegation Framework
description: A guide to handing over a responsibility with clear ownership. Choose a suitable task and colleague, agree the desired outcome and decision-making authority, and set checkpoints appropriate to their experience. Useful when too much work depends on you or a team member is ready for more responsibility.

title: Public Speaking Basics
description: A video on managing nerves when speaking to a group. Covers rehearsing the opening, pacing your delivery, using pauses, and recovering when you lose your place. Useful when you have prepared your material but anxiety makes it difficult to deliver confidently.

title: Mindful Breathing
description: A 2-minute guided breathing exercise to pause and settle your attention before a stressful workplace moment. Useful before a presentation, difficult conversation, or demanding meeting when you feel tense or rushed. Practise slowing down and noticing your breathing before returning to the situation.

title: Effective 1-on-1s
description: A guide to making regular meetings with direct reports useful for both people. Build a shared agenda around progress, obstacles, support, and development, then capture agreed follow-up actions. Useful when one-to-ones feel like status reporting or important concerns only surface after they have grown.

title: Negotiation Strategies
description: A video on navigating a negotiation once the conversation begins. Explore the other party's interests, ask questions about objections, and make conditional trades instead of conceding immediately. Uses salary and contract discussions to show how to respond when an initial proposal is rejected or the discussion stalls.

title: Inbox Zero Masterclass
description: A video demonstrating a repeatable routine for processing a crowded inbox. Group email checks into planned sessions, separate actionable messages from reference material, and track replies that need follow-up. Useful when repeated inbox checking fragments your day or important requests disappear among unread messages.

title: Prioritizing Competing Deadlines
description: A worksheet for deciding what deserves attention when several tasks all feel urgent. Compare impact, deadlines, dependencies, and the consequences of delay, then choose what to do first and what to renegotiate. Useful when you are busy throughout the day but your most important commitments keep slipping.

title: Personal Productivity Audit
description: Review a recent working week using your calendar and a simple activity log. Identify patterns in meetings, interruptions, rework, and focused work, then choose one change to try. Useful when you regularly run out of time but cannot explain where your effort is going.

title: Reducing Recurring Meeting Load
description: A guide to reviewing recurring meetings against the decisions or outcomes they support. Consider which meetings need your attendance, could be shorter or less frequent, or could become written updates, and agree changes with the people involved. Useful when recurring commitments leave little space for your own work.

title: Setting Workload Boundaries
description: A guide to responding when a new request exceeds your available capacity. Explain existing commitments, offer realistic options, and agree which deadline or priority should change. Useful when you keep saying yes to colleagues or your manager and then work late or miss promises.

title: Following Up Without Micromanaging
description: A video on staying informed after you have delegated work. Agree progress signals and escalation points, use planned check-ins, and distinguish a different working style from a genuine risk to the outcome. Useful when you repeatedly chase updates or take work back from a capable colleague.

title: Coaching Instead of Giving Answers
description: A video showing how to help a team member think through a problem and own their next action. Use open questions to explore their goal, options, and reasoning before offering advice. Useful when colleagues bring every decision to you and you want to build their confidence and independence.

title: Preparing Constructive Feedback
description: Prepare a feedback conversation using a specific observation, its impact, and the change you want to discuss. Separate what you saw from assumptions about intent, and write an opening that invites the other person's perspective. Useful when a colleague's behaviour needs addressing and you are unsure how to raise it clearly.

title: Handling Defensive Reactions to Feedback
description: A video on responding when someone disputes feedback, becomes upset, or shifts blame during the conversation. Practise acknowledging their reaction, checking your understanding, and returning to specific observations and a shared next step. Useful when a feedback discussion becomes tense and you struggle to keep it constructive.

title: Making Use of Difficult Feedback
description: A reflection exercise for feedback you have received that feels unfair, vague, or uncomfortable. Record what was actually said, identify questions that would clarify it, and choose a useful action to test. Useful when you keep replaying criticism or feel an immediate urge to defend yourself.

title: Addressing Repeated Missed Commitments
description: A guide to following up when a team member continues to miss agreed commitments after an earlier conversation. Review specific examples, explore barriers and support needs, and agree clear expectations and a review point. Useful when initial feedback has not led to a sustained change in performance.

title: Structuring a Clear Presentation
description: A planning worksheet for turning a collection of information into a presentation with a clear purpose. Define what the audience should understand or decide, select supporting evidence, and build a concise opening, sequence, and conclusion. Useful when your material feels scattered or your audience struggles to find the main point.

title: Answering Challenging Questions
description: A video on handling questions during a presentation or stakeholder meeting. Practise pausing, clarifying the question, giving a direct answer, and acknowledging what you need to check. Useful when unexpected challenges lead you to ramble, become defensive, or make claims you cannot support.

title: Writing Concise Updates for Senior Leaders
description: A guide to writing short stakeholder updates that make progress, risks, and decisions easy to understand. Lead with the outcome or request, include only the evidence needed, and make ownership and next steps explicit. Useful when detailed emails or reports leave senior colleagues unclear about what you need from them.

title: Listening Before Solving
description: A practice exercise for conversations where you tend to interrupt, assume the problem, or offer advice too quickly. Summarize what you heard, check your interpretation, and ask what support the other person wants. Useful when colleagues say they do not feel heard or your attempts to help miss their concern.

title: Mediating Conflict Between Colleagues
description: A guide for a manager helping two colleagues resolve a working disagreement. Hear each perspective, establish shared expectations for the discussion, and facilitate an agreement about future behaviour and responsibilities. Useful when tension between team members is disrupting collaboration and you need to act as a neutral facilitator.

title: Disagreeing Without Escalating
description: A video on expressing a different view when you are personally involved in a disagreement. Explain your concern using specific facts, ask about the other person's reasoning, and identify a shared outcome to work toward. Useful when challenging a colleague's proposal feels confrontational or discussions turn into arguments.

title: Rebuilding Trust After a Misunderstanding
description: A reflection and conversation-planning exercise for a working relationship strained by a specific incident. Consider your contribution, prepare an acknowledgement of the impact, and choose a concrete follow-through commitment. Useful when a disagreement has ended but a colleague remains distant or reluctant to rely on you.

title: Preparing a Salary Negotiation
description: A worksheet to prepare before asking for a pay increase. Gather evidence of your contribution, clarify the outcome you want, consider available compensation information, and plan how to open the discussion. Useful when you want to make a well-supported request but have not yet organized your case or alternatives.

title: Negotiating Competing Team Priorities
description: A guide to reaching agreement when teams compete for the same people, time, or delivery capacity. Surface each team's underlying needs, make dependencies and tradeoffs visible, and agree ownership of the resulting commitments. Useful when cross-team requests keep creating incompatible promises or repeated disputes over whose work comes first.

title: Switching Off After Work
description: An exercise for creating a repeatable end-of-day routine. Capture unfinished work, identify the next action for tomorrow, and decide how to handle work messages outside agreed hours. Useful when you keep mentally revisiting tasks or checking email during personal time, even after the working day has ended.

title: Checking In on Team Wellbeing
description: A guide to opening a supportive conversation with a team member whose workload or behaviour suggests they may be struggling. Ask about their experience, listen without assuming the cause, and agree practical workplace support and a follow-up. Useful when you have noticed a change but are uncertain how to raise your concern respectfully.

title: Rebuilding Focus After Interruptions
description: A video on returning to a task after messages, calls, or unplanned questions break your concentration. Leave a short restart note, capture incoming requests, and adjust notifications or availability signals to reduce repeated switching. Useful when you have time set aside but struggle to regain momentum once interrupted.
